notes.5: (a) Only the weakest candidates failed to identify the component as a lamp. (b) (i) Many candidates correctly calculated the current in the circuit and gained full credit; others would have scored more if they had shown their method of working. (ii) Many candidates did not realise that the readings on the ammeters would be the same as that in (b)(i) . (c) (i) The majority of candidates knew the correct symbol for a voltmeter, but far fewer were able to draw it correctly connected across the resistor. (ii) Candidates were not penalised again for any mistakes carried forward from (b)(i) .
notes.7: The majority of candidates scored the first marking point, but many thought that a sound wave was a transverse wave and a surface water wave was a longitudinal wave. 16 Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics June 2013
notes.10: (a) Most candidates were successful, but many tried to read too much into a straightforward item and attempted to write an equation based on the efficiency equation. (b) Despite their problems with part (a) , the vast majority recognised that for a high efficiency the wasted energy needed to be kept as low as possible. (c) This was probably one of the best scoring questions on the paper, with the majority of candidates gaining most or all of the available credit.
notes.11: (a) Only the very best candidates gained any credit for this question. Very few candidates were able to see the link between alpha particles and the distances involved meaning that the only radiation detected would be background. However in part (b) many candidates mentioned that alpha particles could only travel a few centimetres in air. (b) Most candidates scored in part (i) by stating that the detection rate would decrease, but were let down by weak explanations in (ii) .
notes.2a: Many candidates thought the barometer was filled with water.
notes.2b: Many candidates thought that the space above the liquid was occupied by air.
notes.2d: Many candidates seemed to have a poor understanding of how the barometer worked.
notes.2e: Many candidates thought that the liquid level would rise if air leaked into the space above the liquid.
notes.3a: The majority of candidates gained credit for this section.
notes.3b: Descriptions were generally poor, with most candidates gaining only partial credit, usually for the idea that the molecules move apart during melting.
notes.3c: Most candidates knew freezing point, but a large number thought that this was 1 ºC for ice turning into water.
notes.4a: Only the better candidates seemed able to explain why metals were good conductors. A large number of weaker candidates failed to score on this part.
notes.4b: Most candidates gained credit for this section, as the majority recognised that the rod would become charged.
notes.6a: The majority of candidates scored some credit for their description of how to permanently magnetise a steel rod.
notes.6b: Most candidates correctly identified the force between a N and S pole.
notes.6c: Most candidates correctly stated the induced poles on the iron rod.
notes.6d: A large number of candidates thought there would be an attractive force between the magnet and the rod.
notes.8ai: A number of candidates only ticked one box. This was usually the box indicating that sound travels through air.
notes.8aii: The majority of candidates recognised that sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
notes.8bi: A number of candidates failed to state that the first sound heard would travel direct from the explosion.
notes.8bii: Many candidates scored most or all of the available credit for calculating the speed of sound. The most common error was in using 6.0 seconds as a time instead of 0.6 seconds.
notes.9ai: Many candidates found the calculation involving the transformer equation difficult but could possibly have gained some more credit if they had clearly set out their method of working.
notes.9aii: Many candidates recognised that the lamp would be dimmer, but failed to state that the voltage would be lower.
notes.9bi: Very few candidates stated that the transformer was used to increase voltage.
notes.9bii: Many candidates did not realise that a step-down transformer was needed.
